title: Beyond RAG: A Relational Context Engine That Cuts Token Burn — Unblocked
talk_summary: Speaker presents a context engine that combines semantic retrieval with structured, relational queries over scattered engineering context such as PRs, docs, and Slack to produce task-specific bundles. He demos open-source components for schema discovery, identity resolution, query synthesis, validation, self-correction, and A/B testing context bundles.

takeaways.what_they_do: The context engine pulls code, docs, PRs, and conversations into a grounded, intent-specific bundle with links for follow-up retrieval.
takeaways.evidence_quote: unblock now delivers a very comprehensive but taskspecific context bundle for this task
takeaways.numbers: Cited $1.29 and ~1.5 min with context engine vs up to $2.60 and ~3 min without; ~50% cost reduction

takeaways.technique: Structured query layer over operational data
takeaways.what_they_do: They translate natural-language questions into structured queries for relational/temporal questions that vector search cannot answer well, such as merged PRs last week or top reviewers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: retrieval has two halves essentially. We've got semantic retrieval

takeaways.technique: Validate LLM-generated queries and inject constraints
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat generated queries as untrusted, block dangerous operators, hide sensitive fields from the model, and inject tenant constraints server-side.
takeaways.evidence_quote: query could contain really dangerous operators like the function operator

takeaways.what_they_do: Validation or database errors are fed back to the LLM with a maximum retry count; they also add full-text search when exact matching fails.
takeaways.evidence_quote: take that error and just loop it back in to the LLM and have the LLM kind of self-correct

takeaways.what_they_do: They sample documents to infer schema/enums/indexes and use fuzzy matching for identities, reserving the LLM only as a tiebreaker.
takeaways.evidence_quote: really really far just using traditional procedural methods

takeaways.technique: A/B test context bundles on the same task
takeaways.what_they_do: Their open-source simulator creates a context bundle and runs an A/B test against the same task to show the benefit of having that context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: run an AB test against the same task and show you the benefits
